chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to me, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, from his father, from his grandfather, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
There are four rivers from Paradise: The Euphrates, the Nile, Sihran, and Jehran. The Euphrates is water in this world and the Hereafter, the Nile is honey, Sihran is wine, and Jehran is milk.
ai.seo_question: What are the four rivers of Paradise and what do they provide?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith establishes a cosmological link between earthly geography and celestial rewards, identifying the Euphrates, Nile, Sihwan, and Jihwan as earthly counterparts to Paradise's rivers. While the Nile, Sihwan, and Jihwan are associated with honey, wine, and milk respectively, the Euphrates is uniquely distinguished as providing pure water in both the dunya and the akhirah, reflecting its enduring spiritual significance in Shia tradition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-116 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Hilal, on the authority of Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

There are four Heavenly rivers: The Euphrates, the Nile, Sihran and Jehran. The Euphrates provides water in this world and the Hereafter. The Nile provides honey. Sehran provides wine and Jehran provides milk.”
